# LLMSpy

> A local reverse proxy that records the LLM API calls an app makes and shows each one in a web UI: the prompt, the system message, the tools, the reply and the token counts. An app is pointed at it by its base URL setting (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`); requests are forwarded unchanged and a copy is kept. This file is the reference for AI agents and scripts and describes the repository it ships in; `README.md` is the human guide.

## What it does and does not do

- One HTTP server, on `http://127.0.0.1:8080` by default, serves three things: `/<upstream>/...` is forwarded to an LLM API, `/ping`, `/events` and `/api/*` serve the captured traffic, and anything else is a file of the built web UI.
- Forwarding is a byte-for-byte passthrough, chunk by chunk, so streamed replies still stream to the app. LLMSpy never changes a request or a response.
- It keeps calls in a SQLite file, `~/.llmspy/llmspy.db` (Docker: the `llmspy-data` volume), so they survive a restart. Calls older than `LLMSPY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 7) are removed at startup and every hour. A running call is written when it starts, when its response headers arrive and when it ends; the updates in between are held in memory. A call still running when LLMSpy stopped gets `error: "interrupted: LLMSpy stopped before the call ended"` and `timings.end` set to when its last data arrived.
- `authorization` and `x-api-key` headers are masked in what it records (`Bearer ••••abcd`: the scheme and the last 4 characters of a long key). Prompts, replies and every other header are recorded as sent.
- A call is recorded as soon as its request body has arrived, updated when the response headers arrive, and completed when the exchange ends: when the response has been sent in full, the upstream failed, or the client hung up. Until then `timings.end` is absent. A streamed reply (`text/event-stream`, not compressed) is also updated at most every 500 ms with what has arrived so far; any other reply body stays empty until the exchange ends.
- It does not intercept traffic (no MITM, no CA certificate). An app that has no base URL setting can not be watched.
- It is for local development. It is not authenticated and must not be reachable from other machines.

## Run and stop

From the repository root (`npm install` once first, except for Docker). Running without Docker needs Node.js 26 or later (`engines` in `package.json`); the Docker image brings its own.

| How | Start | Stop |
|---|---|---|
| Docker (runs in the background, restarts with Docker) | `npm run start:docker` (`docker compose up -d --build`) | `npm run stop:docker` (`docker compose down`) |
| Built, local | `npm run build`, then `npm start` | `npm run stop`, from any terminal |
| Development, with reload | `npm run dev` (UI also on `http://localhost:3000`) | Ctrl+C in its terminal |

- Ready when `GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/ping` answers `200`. `npm start` and `npm run dev` stay in the foreground: run them in the background and poll `/ping`.
- All three use port 8080. Stop one before starting another; a second start on a taken port fails with `EADDRINUSE` and exits `1`.
- `npm start` writes `~/.llmspy/llmspy.pid` (`{"pid", "url"}`) once it listens. `npm run stop` stops that process only if `/ping` at that URL reports the same pid, so a stale file is removed and nothing else is killed. It exits `0` when LLMSpy is stopped or was not running. It does not stop Docker or `npm run dev`.
- `npm start` prints the database file and how long calls are kept (`Calls kept 7 days in …`), then the base URL of each upstream. A bad `LLMSPY_UPSTREAMS` or `LLMSPY_RETENTION_DAYS` prints the reason and exits `1`.

## Point an app at it

Set the app's base URL to LLMSpy plus the upstream's path prefix, then start the app (most read the variable only at startup):

| Prefix | Forwards to | Base URL setting |
|---|---|---|
| `/anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/anthropic` |
| `/openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/openai/v1` |

- The rest of the path and the query are appended to the upstream's URL: `/anthropic/v1/messages` goes to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`. The OpenAI SDKs expect `/v1` in their base URL; the Anthropic SDK does not.
- The app's API key is sent through to the provider as usual. LLMSpy needs no key.
- An app in another container reaches the proxy at `http://host.docker.internal:8080/<prefix>`, or by service name in the same compose project. Forwarding answers any `Host`; only the traffic endpoints below are limited to loopback.
- To group an app's calls into a project, put `/@<project>` in front of the prefix: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/@my-app/anthropic`. It is not forwarded, and sets the record's `project`; without it the project is `general`. Project names follow the same rule as upstream names (below); any other name gets the `404` for an unknown prefix.

## Configuration

Environment variables, read once at startup:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PROXY_PORT` | `8080` | Port for everything. Not passed into Docker: there it is always `8080` |
| `LLMSPY_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Interface to listen on. The Docker image sets `0.0.0.0` and compose publishes the port on `127.0.0.1` only |
| `LLMSPY_UPSTREAMS` | empty | Extra or replacement upstreams, as comma-separated `name=url` |
| `LLMSPY_RETENTION_DAYS` | `7` | Days to keep calls, a whole number; `0` keeps them until cleared. Passed into Docker from `.env` |

`LLMSPY_UPSTREAMS`:

- Each entry adds the prefix `/<name>`. A name that is already there (`anthropic`, `openai`) is replaced.
- Names are lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit. `api`, `assets`, `events` and `ping` are refused.
- URLs must be `http` or `https`. A path in the URL is kept and the request path is appended: `gw=https://gateway.example/v1` sends `/gw/messages` to `https://gateway.example/v1/messages`.
- Set it in the shell or in `.env` at the repo root (next to `compose.yaml`). `npm start`, `npm run dev` and `docker compose up` all read `.env`; in local runs a variable already set in the shell wins. `.env` is read at start: restart LLMSpy (or rerun `npm run start:docker`) after changing it.
- Inside the container `localhost` is the container: an upstream on the host is `http://host.docker.internal:<port>`. Locally it is `localhost`, so a `.env` with `host.docker.internal` upstreams is for Docker only.

```bash
LLMSPY_UPSTREAMS=ollama=http://localhost:11434,llmock=http://127.0.0.1:8001 npm start
```

## Reading captured traffic

| Route | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /ping` | `200 {"status":"running","message","port","pid","timestamp"}`; `port` is the port really bound |
| `GET /api/requests` | `200`, a JSON array of the summary of every record, newest first (below). `?project=<name>` keeps that project's; `?q=<text>` keeps those whose `host`, `path`, request body or response body holds the text, ignoring case; `?since=<time>` keeps those whose `timings.start` is at or after the time, given as an ISO time (`2026-11-15T10:00:00Z`; without a zone it is local time) or epoch milliseconds; `?model=<text>` keeps those whose `llm.model` holds the text, ignoring case (`model=sonnet`); `?status=<code>` keeps those whose `response.status` is that code (`429`) or in that class (`5xx`), so never a call with no response; `?failed=1` keeps the failed calls: those with an `error`, a `response.status` of 400 or above, or an `llm.error` (the same calls the UI's Failed chip shows); `?limit=<n>` keeps only the newest `n` of those left; `?full=1` returns the full records instead of summaries, in the same order (running calls as they are so far). Any of them together keep calls that match all. A value that can not be read (a project name that can not exist, a `since` that is not a time, an empty `model`, a `status` that is not three digits or a digit and `xx`, a `limit` that is not a whole number above 0, a `failed` or `full` other than `1`) gets `400` with a plain-text message |
| `GET /api/stats` | `200`, counts over the calls `GET /api/requests` would list with the same `project`, `q`, `since`, `model`, `status` and `failed` (read and refused the same way; `limit` and `full` get `400`): `{"calls","running","failed","tokens":{"input","output","cacheRead","cacheWrite"},"latencyMs":{"p50","p95","max"},"byModel":{...},"byProject":{...}}`. `running` counts calls with no `timings.end`; `failed` as `?failed=1`. `tokens` adds up `llm.usage` (a count a call did not report adds 0; a running call adds what it has so far); Anthropic's `input` leaves out cached tokens and OpenAI's includes them, so mixing providers mixes the two. `latencyMs` is over ended calls only, by nearest rank, and `null` when none has ended. `byModel` (keyed by `llm.model`, `none` for calls with no model) and `byProject` give the same fields for each, without their own `byModel`/`byProject` |
| `GET /api/requests/<id>` | `200`, the full record; `404` when no record has that `id`. `?wait=<seconds>` (a whole number from 1 to 300, else `400`) holds the answer while the call is running: it comes when the call ends, or when the seconds run out with the call so far (no `timings.end`; still `200`). An ended call, or an unknown `id`, is answered at once; a call deleted or cleared while you wait gets `404` |
| `GET /api/requests/<id>/conversation` | `200 text/markdown`: the call as you would read it, in full. A header line (time, project, status or `running`, latency, tokens, stop reason), then `## System`, `## Tools`, one section per message (`## User`, `## Assistant`, `## Tool`), `## Assistant (reply)` and `## Error` when there is one (a body that could not be read is named there, and what could be read is still shown). Thinking is quoted, tool calls and results are in code fences, images are `[image]`. `404` when no record has that `id`, or when the call was not read as an LLM API call (read the record instead). Takes `?wait=<seconds>` as the record does; on timeout the header says `running` |
| `GET /api/upstreams` | `200`, a JSON array of `{"name","target"}` in configuration order; any user name or password in `target` is removed |
| `POST /api/clear` | `200 {"success":true}`: every record is deleted (from the database file too) and every `/events` client is sent a `clear` event. No body needed. With `?project=<name>` only that project's records are deleted; `400` when the name can not be a project |
| `DELETE /api/requests/<id>` | `204`: that record is deleted and every `/events` client is sent a `delete` event; `404` when no record has that `id`. A call still running is stored again when it next updates |
| `GET /events` | Server-Sent Events: on connect the summary of every stored record, newest first, then a record's summary each time it is captured or updated. Each summary is one `data: <summary JSON>` line with no `event:` name; read the full record from `GET /api/requests/<id>`. When the records are cleared it sends `event: clear` with `data: {}`: drop every record you hold; `data: {"project":"<name>"}` when only one project was: drop that project's records. When one record is deleted it sends `event: delete` with `data: {"id":"<id>"}`: drop that record. A call arrives several times with the same `id` (more often while a reply streams): replace by `id`, and treat it as finished once `timings.end` is set |

- A query string is ignored, except `project` on `/api/clear`, `wait` on the two reads of one call, and the parameters above on `/api/requests` and `/api/stats`; an unknown parameter is ignored too (`/api/requests?max=1` returns every summary). Otherwise paths must match exactly; `/api/requests/` (trailing slash) is answered `404`. There is no paging: narrow with `since`, `project` and `limit`.
- These routes answer only requests whose `Host` is `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` (with any port), or the address in `LLMSPY_HOST` when that is not `0.0.0.0`/`::`. A request with an `Origin` header must also come from the same origin as its `Host`. Anything else gets `403` with a plain-text message. curl, scripts and SDKs send no `Origin` and pass when they call `127.0.0.1`; a call from another container (`Host: llmspy` or `host.docker.internal`) gets `403`.
- A record can be large (a coding agent's request is often around 1 MB), which is why the list routes send summaries: read only the records you need, and use `full=1` with `since` or `limit`, not on its own.

## Record shape

Each record from `/api/requests/<id>`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Random UUID |
| `timestamp` | ISO time the request arrived |
| `project` | From `/@<project>` in front of the prefix, else `general` |
| `provider` | The upstream name, from the path prefix |
| `host` | The upstream host it was forwarded to |
| `method`, `path` | As sent upstream (`path` includes the query) |
| `headers` | Request headers, keys masked, hop-by-hop headers removed |
| `body` | Request body, decompressed and decoded as UTF-8 text (JSON is a string: parse it) |
| `response` | `{"status","headers","body"}`, body decompressed and decoded. Absent until the response headers arrive, and when the upstream never answered; `body` is `""` until the call ends, except for a streamed reply, which holds what has arrived so far |
| `timings` | `{"start","firstByte"?,"lastData"?,"end"?}`, epoch ms; `firstByte` is when the response headers arrived, `lastData` when the latest chunk of a streamed reply arrived (only for the uncompressed streams updated while they arrive); no `end` while the call is still running. On a running stream, `lastData` shows how long it has been quiet |
| `latency` | `end - start`, ms; absent while the call is still running |
| `error` | Set when the exchange failed: `Upstream request failed: …` (never reached; the app got `502`), `Upstream response failed: …` (the reply broke off), `Client closed the connection before the response finished`, `interrupted: LLMSpy stopped before the call ended` |
| `llm` | The call read as an LLM API call, below. Absent when the path is not one LLMSpy knows |

A streamed response body is the raw SSE text. A body that can not be decompressed is replaced by `[LLMSpy could not decode this body: …]`.

A summary, in `/api/requests` and `/events`, has the record's `id`, `timestamp`, `project`, `provider`, `host`, `method`, `path`, `timings`, `latency` and `error`, plus `response: {"status"}` and `llm: {"model","usage","error"}` when the record has them. It has no headers or bodies.

### `llm`

Present for `POST` requests whose path ends in `/v1/messages` (`format: "anthropic-messages"`), `/chat/completions` (`"openai-chat"`) or `/responses` (`"openai-responses"`), whatever the upstream's name. While the call is running it holds what the request says (model, system, tools, messages), plus, for a streamed reply, the reply read so far; the reply is complete when the call ends. The same shape for every format:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `format` | One of the three above |
| `model` | The model that answered, else the one asked for |
| `stream` | Whether the reply was streamed |
| `system` | The system prompt or instructions, as one string |
| `messages` | The conversation sent, oldest first: `[{"role","parts"}]`, `role` is `user`, `assistant` or `tool` |
| `tools` | `[{"name","description"?}]`; the schemas are only in `body` |
| `output` | The reply as one message (`role: "assistant"`), reassembled if streamed |
| `stopReason` | As the provider sent it (`end_turn`, `tool_use`, `stop`, `length`, …) |
| `usage` | `{"input"?,"output"?,"cacheRead"?,"cacheWrite"?,"reasoning"?}` as the provider counts them; Anthropic's `input` excludes cached tokens, OpenAI's includes them |
| `error` | `{"type"?,"message"}`: an error the provider sent inside a `2xx` reply, such as an `error` event part-way through a stream |
| `parseError` | Set when a body could not be read; the fields that could be read are still there |

A part is one of:

- `{"type":"text","text"}`
- `{"type":"thinking","text"}`
- `{"type":"tool_call","id","name","input"}`, where `input` is parsed JSON when possible
- `{"type":"tool_result","id","content","isError"?}`, matched to its call by `id`
- `{"type":"image"}`, with the data left out
- `{"type":"other","raw"}`, a block LLMSpy has no view for, as sent

Only `2xx` responses are parsed. For a `4xx`/`5xx` call, `llm` has the request fields but no `output`, `stopReason` or `usage`: read `response.status` and `response.body`.

## Errors

| What the app gets | Why | In the record |
|---|---|---|
| `404 text/plain` `LLMSpy: no upstream for <path>. Known prefixes: …` | The first path segment is not an upstream | Nothing recorded |
| `502 text/plain` `LLMSpy could not reach <origin>: …` | DNS, connection or TLS failure to the upstream | `error`, no `response` |
| The connection is cut | The upstream's reply broke off part-way | `error`, `response` with what arrived |
| The provider's own status and body | Anything the provider answered, `4xx`/`5xx` included | `response` as sent |
| `403 text/plain` | A traffic endpoint called with another `Host` or `Origin` (above) | Nothing recorded |

## Recipes

The last call's prompt and reply, without `jq`:

```bash
node -e "
  const base = 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests';
  fetch(base).then((res) => res.json()).then(async ([s]) => {
    const r = s && (await (await fetch(base + '/' + s.id)).json());
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ status: r?.response?.status, error: r?.error, llm: r?.llm }, null, 2));
  });"
```

With `jq`: `id=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests | jq -r '.[0].id'); curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests/$id" | jq '.llm | {model, system, messages, output, usage}'`.

Read the last call as text, the shortest way to see what an agent sent and got back: `id=$(curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests?limit=1' | jq -r '.[0].id'); curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests/$id/conversation"`.

Find the calls that mention something: `curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests?q=get_weather'`, then read each by `id`.

Find what went wrong: `curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests?failed=1&limit=10'` lists the newest failed calls; read one's `error`, `response.status` and `llm.error` in its summary, then the record or `/conversation` for the detail. `?status=429` finds the rate-limited ones, `?model=haiku&failed=1` one model's failures.

How much a task cost and how slow it was: note `since` as below, run the app, then `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/stats?since=$since"` for the calls, failures, tokens and p50/p95 latency, in all and per model. Read `/api/requests` with the same parameters to see which calls they were.

The last 3 calls in full: `curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests?full=1&limit=3'`.

Check what an app sends for one task, without clearing anyone's calls: note the time (`since=$(date +%s%3N)`, or `Date.now()`), run the app, then read `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests?since=$since&full=1"` (newest first, so reverse it for the order the calls were made in). Add `&project=<name>` when other apps send traffic at the same time.

Wait for a call to end: find its `id` (`GET /api/requests?since=<when you started>&limit=1`, or the first summary on `/events`), then `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/requests/$id/conversation?wait=120"` answers once it ends; use `/api/requests/$id?wait=120` for the record. If the answer still has no `timings.end` (or the Markdown header says `running`), the wait ran out: ask again. Waiting for a call that has not been sent yet is not built in: poll `GET /api/requests?since=<when you started>` until a summary shows up.

Without an API key: `npm run mock` starts mock LLM APIs (Anthropic Messages on `127.0.0.1:8001`, OpenAI Chat Completions on `127.0.0.1:8002`). Start LLMSpy with `LLMSPY_UPSTREAMS=llmock=http://127.0.0.1:8001,llmock-openai=http://127.0.0.1:8002`, then `node scripts/mock-traffic.mjs` sends one call of each kind (tool call, `max_tokens`, refusal, `429`, stream error, dropped stream). The README lists the prompt markers that pick each reply.

## Do not

- Do not set `LLMSPY_HOST` to `0.0.0.0` outside Docker, or publish the Docker port as anything but `127.0.0.1:8080:8080`: forwarding and the UI would be open to the network.
- Do not save or commit captured records: they hold whole prompts and replies, and the masked key's last 4 characters.
- Do not rely on records older than `LLMSPY_RETENTION_DAYS`.
- Do not read or change `llmspy.db` directly: use the routes above. Its layout is not part of this reference.
